passage: Tushar had ten days until the next Maths test and a 30 out of 100 from the last one. His cousin's wedding would swallow both weekends, and his phone screen was cracked, so lesson videos were out. Sarita Didi, home for the holidays, went through the old paper with him. "Stop aiming for 80. Where are the easy marks?" They sorted the questions: one-mark definitions, simple linear equations, the area formulas. Together those were worth nearly twenty marks, and Tushar had dropped most of them. "Get 45. Just those three types, every day for ten days." He did twenty minutes each morning before the wedding chaos began. On test day he finished the easy section first, calm for once. He got 47. It was the first Maths paper he had wanted to show anyone.

qa.q: What did Tushar score on the new test?
How did Tushar feel on test day compared with before?
qa.a: He felt calm for once, and afterwards proud enough to want to show the paper to someone 😊.

qa.q: What should Tushar aim for after the 47?
qa.a: Add the next easiest question type and aim a little higher, so the routine grows without becoming overwhelming.

qa.q: How might Sarita Didi see Tushar's 47?
qa.a: She is likely pleased and proud that the small target worked, even with the wedding and the cracked phone in the way.

grounding: Shows a student with little time aiming for 45 instead of 80 by mastering only the easiest question types, and building confidence.

passage: Chinmay pinned his Chemistry test to the wall of the small room above his father's tailoring shop in Dadar: 30 out of 100. His first plan, scribbled that night, said "80 next time!!" and listed every chapter. It lasted two days. Then Indu from the third floor, who had topped Chemistry last year, glanced at the list and snorted. "You'll drown. What do you already half know?" Naming compounds, balancing simple equations, the definitions list. "Get those perfect. Aim for 45." So he did: fifteen balancing questions a night, the naming chart stuck above his bed. In the next test he got 44, and for the first time he knew exactly which marks were his. The following week he added mole calculations to the wall.

qa.q: What score was Chinmay's first plan aiming for?
What might Chinmay have felt when his first plan collapsed after two days?
qa.a: He probably felt overwhelmed and discouraged, facing every chapter at once with nowhere to start.

qa.q: Why did aiming for 45 work better than aiming for 80?
qa.a: It narrowed the work to a few question types he half knew, so he could get them right, see real progress and keep a routine going.

qa.q: How might Indu see Chinmay's first plan?
qa.a: Indu finds it unrealistic enough to snort at, and wants to steer Chinmay toward a target that won't drown him.
